task.description:
Validate src/design/iss0626-handoff-bookkeeping-repair.md before BACKEND-DEV implements the repair script. This design covers a safe-mechanical subset (H002, H008, H010, H006-partial, H001-encoding-subset) of GH-594/ISS-0626's handoff bookkeeping debt -- ~2000 pre-existing JSON files across the project's history. A mistake in this script is expensive: it operates on the project's own audit trail.

ORCH already independently verified: (1) H002/H006's detection logic matches tools/lint_handoffs.py's actual source exactly (isinstance(result, str) for H002; result.status only, never top-level status, for H006), (2) found and CORRECTED a real scope-drift in the design's original section 4.2 -- it proposed also renaming a top-level status field of FAILED, but lint_handoffs.py never actually validates the top-level status field against any enum (TERMINAL_OK is defined but dead code) -- so that rename would have been the script inventing its own fix target rather than closing a real lint_handoffs.py finding. Corrected in commit e1910eb (sections 4.2, 4.3, section 10 summary). (3) Confirmed python tools/lint_design_artefact.py exits 0.

YOUR JOB: run your own full independent validation -- do not just trust ORCH's correction was complete or sufficient. In particular:
1. Read the ENTIRE design fresh, including the corrected sections 4.2/4.3, and confirm no OTHER place in the document still references a top-level status rename (search for 'top-level' yourself).
2. Independently verify EVERY category's detection predicate against tools/lint_handoffs.py's actual source (not just H002/H006 which ORCH already checked) -- H008's BOM check, H010's registry-membership check, and confirm the H001 category truly has no discrete encoding-vs-structural split in lint_handoffs.py's own output (design section 7 claims this).
3. Scrutinize section 0's four operating constraints (dry-run-first, idempotent, self-verifying write via C-3's re-parse-then-atomic-replace, category isolation with fixed pass ordering) for genuine soundness -- is the C-4 pass ordering (H008 -> H001-encoding -> H002 -> H006 -> H010) actually correct given what each pass reads/writes? Could any ordering produce a wrong result (e.g. running H002 before H001-encoding-subset on a file that needs both)?
4. Scrutinize section 5's H001 byte-diff gate (`_only_known_corruption_bytes_differ`) -- is a difflib.SequenceMatcher-based opcode comparison against a fixed corruption-signature table actually sufficient to catch every possible 'something else also changed' case, or could a subtle diff-alignment edge case slip an unintended change past the gate?
5. Confirm section 3 (H010)'s 'purely additive, no invented fields' claim holds under your own reading -- especially the duplicate-handoff_id guard (3.4) and the missing-required-field skip (3.3).
6. Confirm the 6 test specs in section 9 are genuinely mutation-checkable (each has an explicit 'what happens if reverted' check) and that the negative/companion cases (H002's string-that-round-trips-to-a-string, H010's missing-field skip, H001's Fixture B/C) actually exercise the rejection paths, not just the happy path.
7. Confirm scope discipline against section 8's explicit exclusions -- no design element reaches into H003/H004/H005/H006-CONDITIONAL/H007/H009/H013/H001-structural.
acceptance_criteria: Every category detection predicate verified against real lint_handoffs.py source
No stale reference to a top-level status rename remains anywhere in the document
C-4 pass ordering verified sound, not just asserted
H001 byte-diff gate scrutinized for genuine robustness
All 6 test specs confirmed genuinely mutation-checkable
Scope discipline against section 8 exclusions confirmed
